plan.planning_summary: Refining route_03 after multiple material_data and compilation failures. Three complementary Fabry-Perot cavity designs proposed with verified IR dielectric material pairs, explicit layer counts, and diagnostic initialization checks. Route 1: 22-layer Ge/ZnS two-cavity design following evidence-based MIR filter topology. Route 2: 20-layer Si3N4/MgF2 alternative material pair with lower absorption in 3-5μm range. Route 3: 18-layer simplified single-cavity with thicker spacer for dual-band merging. All routes include explicit thickness bounds, quarter-wave seeding, and material registry validation steps to prevent prior truncation errors.

routes.title: 22-Layer Ge/ZnS Two-Cavity Fabry-Perot Dual-Band Filter with Validated Material Names
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A two-cavity Fabry-Perot structure with Ge (high-index) and ZnS (low-index) quarter-wave stacks separated by cavity spacer layers can simultaneously transmit both 4.15-4.35μm and 4.55-4.75μm bands while blocking 3.60-4.00μm and 4.85-5.20μm stopbands on CaF2 substrate.
routes.design_principle: Multi-cavity Fabry-Perot bandpass filter using alternating quarter-wave high-low index dielectric layers with computational thickness optimization. Two cavities enable dual-passband shaping from triangular to square profile per evidence on MIR filter design.
routes.proposed_topology: CaF2 substrate | [Ge/ZnS]_4 mirror | Ge cavity spacer | [Ge/ZnS]_3 coupling | Ge cavity spacer | [Ge/ZnS]_4 mirror | Air. Total 22 finite layers (11 Ge + 11 ZnS).
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 22 layers
manufacturing_considerations: Ge and ZnS are conventional depositable IR dielectrics
total thickness should remain under 10μm for stress management
theory_basis: Transfer-matrix method for coherent thin-film interference
Fabry-Perot cavity resonance condition: 2nd = mλ for constructive transmission
Quarter-wave stack reflectance increases with pair count
expected_advantages: Ge/ZnS has high index contrast (~4.0 vs ~2.3) for strong reflectors
Two cavities enable dual-band transmission shaping
22 layers provides sufficient degrees of freedom for optimization
known_risks: Material registry name mismatch caused prior failures - must verify 'Ge' and 'ZnS' are valid identifiers
Ge has absorption edge near 2μm but should be transparent in 3-5μm range
Fabrication tolerance sensitivity increases with layer count
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 22-layer dielectric bandpass filter on CaF2 substrate for dual-band IR transmission. Stack topology: CaF2 | (Ge/ZnS)_4 | Ge_cavity | (Ge/ZnS)_3 | Ge_cavity | (Ge/ZnS)_4 | Air. Initialize all Ge layers at quarter-wave thickness for 4.45μm center wavelength (n_Ge≈4.0, thickness≈278nm). Initialize all ZnS layers at quarter-wave thickness (n_ZnS≈2.3, thickness≈484nm). Initialize both cavity spacers at half-wave thickness (≈556nm). Set thickness search bounds: Ge layers [150, 450]nm, ZnS layers [300, 650]nm, cavity spacers [400, 750]nm. Verify material registry accepts 'Ge' and 'ZnS' as valid identifiers before optimization. Optimize all 22 layer thicknesses to maximize transmittance in 4.15-4.35μm and 4.55-4.75μm bands while minimizing transmittance in 3.60-4.00μm and 4.85-5.20μm bands. Use coherent TMM at normal incidence. Log initialization thickness vector and material lookup results for diagnostic purposes. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3600-4000 nm, 4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm, 4850-5200 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 um and 4.55-4.75 um bands; low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 um and 4.85-5.20 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance in stopbands; high reflectance in passbands. manufacturing constraints: no metal layers; maximum 24 layers; conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials.
routes.revision_reason: Prior route_03 iterations failed due to material_data errors and compilation issues. This revision explicitly validates material registry names ('Ge' and 'ZnS' instead of potentially truncated 'si'), uses evidence-backed Ge/ZnS pair for MIR range, maintains 22-layer two-cavity Fabry-Perot topology with explicit layer count, and adds diagnostic logging for initialization to identify rejection causes.

routes.title: 20-Layer Si3N4/MgF2 Two-Cavity Filter with Lower Absorption Risk
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A two-cavity Fabry-Perot structure with Si3N4 (high-index) and MgF2 (low-index) can achieve dual-band transmission in 4.15-4.35μm and 4.55-4.75μm with lower absorption risk than Ge-based designs in the 3-5μm range.
routes.design_principle: Alternative dielectric material pair with verified IR transparency. Si3N4 and MgF2 have lower absorption coefficients in mid-IR compared to Ge, reducing risk of material_data failures while maintaining sufficient index contrast (~2.0 vs ~1.35) for reflector stacks.
routes.proposed_topology: CaF2 substrate | [Si3N4/MgF2]_4 mirror | Si3N4 cavity spacer | [Si3N4/MgF2]_3 coupling | Si3N4 cavity spacer | [Si3N4/MgF2]_4 mirror | Air. Total 20 finite layers (10 Si3N4 + 10 MgF2).
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 20 layers
manufacturing_considerations: Si3N4 and MgF2 are conventional depositable dielectrics
lower index contrast requires more layers but reduces absorption risk
theory_basis: Transfer-matrix method for coherent thin-film interference
Fabry-Perot cavity resonance with lower-index-contrast materials
expected_advantages: Si3N4 and MgF2 have well-characterized optical constants in material registries
Lower absorption in 3-5μm range reduces material_data failure risk
20 layers provides optimization flexibility while staying under 24-layer limit
known_risks: Lower index contrast (~2.0/1.35 vs ~4.0/2.3) requires more layers for equivalent reflectance
MgF2 may have absorption features beyond 4.5μm that need verification
Dual-band separation may be harder to achieve with lower contrast
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 20-layer dielectric bandpass filter on CaF2 substrate for dual-band IR transmission. Stack topology: CaF2 | (Si3N4/MgF2)_4 | Si3N4_cavity | (Si3N4/MgF2)_3 | Si3N4_cavity | (Si3N4/MgF2)_4 | Air. Initialize all Si3N4 layers at quarter-wave thickness for 4.45μm center wavelength (n_Si3N4≈2.0, thickness≈556nm). Initialize all MgF2 layers at quarter-wave thickness (n_MgF2≈1.35, thickness≈824nm). Initialize both cavity spacers at half-wave thickness (≈1112nm). Set thickness search bounds: Si3N4 layers [350, 750]nm, MgF2 layers [550, 1000]nm, cavity spacers [800, 1400]nm. Verify material registry accepts 'Si3N4' and 'MgF2' as valid identifiers before optimization. Optimize all 20 layer thicknesses to maximize transmittance in 4.15-4.35μm and 4.55-4.75μm bands while minimizing transmittance in 3.60-4.00μm and 4.85-5.20μm bands. Use coherent TMM at normal incidence. Log initialization thickness vector and material lookup results for diagnostic purposes. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3600-4000 nm, 4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm, 4850-5200 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 um and 4.55-4.75 um bands; low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 um and 4.85-5.20 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance in stopbands; high reflectance in passbands. manufacturing constraints: no metal layers; maximum 24 layers; conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials.
routes.revision_reason: Alternative to route_03_refinement_01 in case Ge/ZnS material registry lookup fails. Si3N4/MgF2 pair is commonly available in thin-film material databases with well-characterized IR optical constants. Reduces absorption risk while maintaining two-cavity Fabry-Perot topology. Layer count reduced to 20 to compensate for lower index contrast while staying within 24-layer limit.

routes.title: 18-Layer ThSi2/YF3 Simplified Single-Cavity with Broader Passband
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A simplified single-cavity Fabry-Perot design with ThSi2 (high-index) and YF3 (low-index) can achieve merged dual-band transmission by using a broader passband that covers both 4.15-4.35μm and 4.55-4.75μm ranges with a single resonance peak.
routes.design_principle: Single-cavity design reduces optimization complexity and layer count while using a broader passband to cover both target bands. ThSi2/YF3 material pair offers high index contrast with verified IR transparency. Broader FWHM merges the two passbands into one continuous transmission window.
routes.proposed_topology: CaF2 substrate | [ThSi2/YF3]_4 mirror | ThSi2 cavity spacer | [ThSi2/YF3]_4 mirror | Air. Total 18 finite layers (9 ThSi2 + 9 YF3).
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 18 layers
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance across merged 4.15-4.75μm band
maintain transmittance uniformity across merged passband
manufacturing_considerations: ThSi2 and YF3 are depositable IR dielectrics
theory_basis: Broader passband achieved through reduced mirror reflectance (fewer pairs)
Quarter-wave stack design with cavity resonance
expected_advantages: Fewer layers (18) reduces optimization complexity and material_data failure risk
Broader passband may better accommodate both target bands without precise dual-peak tuning
ThSi2/YF3 pair has high index contrast for strong reflectors with fewer pairs
known_risks: Merged passband may not provide sufficient spectral selectivity between CO and CO2 bands
Single cavity produces triangular rather than square passband profile
ThSi2 material availability in registry may be limited compared to Ge or Si3N4
routes.execution_request_english: Design an 18-layer dielectric bandpass filter on CaF2 substrate for broad IR transmission covering 4.15-4.75μm. Stack topology: CaF2 | (ThSi2/YF3)_4 | ThSi2_cavity | (ThSi2/YF3)_4 | Air. Initialize all ThSi2 layers at quarter-wave thickness for 4.45μm center wavelength (n_ThSi2≈3.0, thickness≈371nm). Initialize all YF3 layers at quarter-wave thickness (n_YF3≈1.5, thickness≈742nm). Initialize cavity spacer at half-wave thickness (≈742nm). Set thickness search bounds: ThSi2 layers [200, 550]nm, YF3 layers [450, 900]nm, cavity spacer [500, 1000]nm. Verify material registry accepts 'ThSi2' and 'YF3' as valid identifiers before optimization. Optimize all 18 layer thicknesses to maximize transmittance across merged 4.15-4.75μm band while minimizing transmittance in 3.60-4.00μm and 4.85-5.20μm stopbands. Use coherent TMM at normal incidence. Log initialization thickness vector and material lookup results for diagnostic purposes. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3600-4000 nm, 4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm, 4850-5200 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 um and 4.55-4.75 um bands; low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 um and 4.85-5.20 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance in stopbands; high reflectance in passbands. manufacturing constraints: no metal layers; maximum 24 layers; conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials.
routes.revision_reason: Fallback route if both Ge/ZnS and Si3N4/MgF2 material pairs fail registry lookup. Single-cavity topology reduces complexity and layer count to 18, providing margin for material availability issues. Broader passband approach trades spectral selectivity for robustness - if dual-band separation proves infeasible, merged band may still meet system requirements. ThSi2/YF3 pair offers alternative high-contrast option.

research_influence: Evidence s2-chunk:CorpusId:237542117 directly motivated Ge/ZnS material pair selection for MIR filters with documented 3-5μm transparency and successful 24-layer fabrication
Evidence s2-chunk:CorpusId:139773493 supported two-cavity Fabry-Perot topology for achieving square passband profiles in NDIR gas sensor applications
Evidence s2-chunk:CorpusId:233820728 informed alternative material pair selection (Si3N4/MgF2, ThSi2/YF3) based on dielectric coating principles for reduced absorption
Prior iteration failures (material_data, compilation errors) directly shaped the diagnostic logging requirements and explicit material name validation steps in all three routes
unresolved_decisions: Material registry availability for Ge, ZnS, Si3N4, MgF2, ThSi2, YF3 identifiers must be verified at execution time - cannot be determined from literature evidence alone
Optimal layer count tradeoff between spectral performance (more layers) and material_data reliability (fewer layers) remains empirical and will be determined by route execution results
Whether dual-band separation requires two-cavity topology or can be achieved with single-cavity broad passband depends on actual transmittance profiles from optimization
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: Stop after the bounded route portfolio is exhausted or further search stagnates. Return every physically verified candidate and report soft objective trade-offs without a performance admission threshold.
